Heavyweight Champ drops

in on Charlotte Games

CHARLOTTE - Heavyweight Boxing
Champion Evander Holyfield set off a frenzy at the
AAU Junior Olympic Games Track and Field
competition in Charlotte, showing up unannounced.
at the track and field competition where his four
kids were competing.

Holyfield arrived outside the UNC
Charlotte Track and Field Center in a blue stretch
limo. As he made his way toward the center’s
press box, hundreds of participants and fans rushed
him. Police officers formed a circle around
Holyfield, finally escorting him safely upstairs.

Holyfield sponsors the Atlanta-based
Quicksilver Track Team, and his four children-
Evander Jr., Ewin, Evette, and Ebonne - are
members of the team. “I just wanted to come to
support my kids,’ Holyfield said. I know when I
was little and was in AAU, I traveled alot for track
and boxing, and my parents weren’t able to travel
with me because they couldn’t afford to. I can
afford it, so I try to come to their meets whenever I
can.”

AAU Officials escorted Holyfield to the
Track’s infield, where he presented medals to the
Champions in several events. Valerie Williams,
17, won the Young Women’s Long Jump. “My
stomach did flip-flops,” Valerie said, her eyes
sparkling as she clutched the medal, “I’m defi-
nitely keeping this one in my site.”
